title: Kai package
description: Shape accepted by BOTH Kai import surfaces — a project kai.json/kai.yml (File → Import…, Project folder) and an Export/Import Configuration file (File → Import…, File). They share this exact schema; only the top-level identity differs (project_name for a project manifest, kai_export for an exported package) — see the manifesto's §1.1. Point an editor at this file with "$schema": "https://kai.app/schema/v1.json" at the top of your kai.json/kai.yml for inline validation and autocomplete.

$schema.description: Optional, ignored by Kai itself — only read by editors for validation/autocomplete. Point it at this file's URL.

project_name.description: Project-manifest identity. Name of the folder Kai creates on import. Absent ⇒ falls back to the imported directory's name. Never present together with kai_export.

icon.description: Icon of the project's/export's root folder. Must be one of the names listed in kai-icons.md — an unrecognized name silently falls back to a generic icon instead of erroring.

cli_path.description: CLI Paths feature. Segment used to address the project's/export's ROOT from `kai <cli_path> ...` — see docs/manifesto/cli-paths.md. Only meaningful as the FIRST segment (global mode requires the root to have one); a project run in local mode (no import) doesn't need it at the root, since local mode has no cross-project namespace to disambiguate.

env_vars.description: Environment variables in the project's/root's scope. Every command under it (and its subfolders) can reference these as {{KEY}}.

kai_export.description: Export-package identity (written by File → Export…; you normally never write this by hand). Presence of this key — or its absence combined with no "id" fields anywhere — is how Kai tells an id-free export apart from a project manifest.

id_free.description: true for every export produced by a current Kai version. Only relevant for the importer's own detection heuristic.

root_folder.description: Export-only. Present only for a folder-scope export: the exported folder's own name/icon, since it's excluded from the folders array below (it's the package's implicit top, mirroring project_name's role in a project manifest).

settings.description: Export-only (global-scope export). Kai's own app preferences (appearance, shortcuts, window, notifications, terminal profiles, environments...). Never written by hand for a project manifest.

folders.description: In a PROJECT manifest: optional, and only ever used to give a subfolder its own icon — {"path": ..., "icon": ...}; the subfolder itself is still created implicitly by a command's/collection's own "folder" key, never by an entry here alone. In an EXPORT package: the full list of subfolders (path + metadata), always written by Kai itself. "path" in either case is relative to the root — never includes project_name/root_folder's own name (a leading "<root name>/" prefix is tolerated but discouraged).

path.description: Required in the top-level folders array (identifies which folder this entry decorates). Absent on root_folder, which has no path of its own.

icon.description: See kai-icons.md for the full valid list.

is_project.description: Internal flag Kai sets on the folder created by importing a project (dynamic-variable scope boundary). A folders[] entry with is_project: true is understood, as a convenience fallback, as "this names the root" when project_name/icon are missing at the top level — prefer the top-level keys instead. Never meaningful on an entry that only decorates a subfolder.

cli_path.description: CLI Paths feature. Segment used to reach this folder from the CLI, e.g. "zephyr" in `kai zephyr env prod`. Absent (default) = this folder is TRANSPARENT in the CLI namespace — invisible as a segment, but doesn't block its own children that do have one (they surface at the nearest opted-in ancestor instead). See docs/manifesto/cli-paths.md.

name.description: Required in practice — an empty name still imports, but is meaningless in the tree and unusable as a hook target.

command.description: Shell only. Supports {{VAR}} interpolation. Required (in practice) when type is "shell".

http_config.description: HTTP only. Required when type is "http".

folder.description: Target subfolder, relative to the root, nestable with "/" (e.g. "Integrations/Shopee"). Omit to place the command directly in the root.

capture_env.description: Must be paired with a non-empty declared_env_vars to capture anything at all.

interactive_terminal.description: Shell only. Mutually distinct from formatted_output — pick one.

formatted_output.description: Shell only. Mutually distinct from interactive_terminal — pick one.

terminal_target.description: Shell only. Name of a Terminal Target (Settings → Terminal Targets) — SENSITIVE: its command_template wraps every command that uses it, so an imported terminal target should always be reviewed before accepting it, not just counted.

params.description: The key is "params", never "parameters" — a kai.json using "parameters" has its parameters silently ignored.

cli_path.description: CLI Paths feature. Segment that makes this command REACHABLE/executable from the CLI, e.g. "env" in `kai zephyr env prod`. The last segment of any usable CLI path always resolves to a command — a folder alone is never executable, only navigable. Absent (default) = not reachable from the CLI at all, GUI-only. See docs/manifesto/cli-paths.md.

name.description: Becomes {{name}} in the command. Use a valid shell-identifier shape (letters/digits/_, starting with a letter or _) if you want it usable as an env var too.

collection.description: select only. Name of a collection in the same package — resolved to an id on import.

initial_dir.description: file only. Used LITERALLY — {{VAR}} is not resolved here.

optional.description: Any type. Field starts hidden behind a checkbox in the GUI form; on a CLI Path, an optional parameter is never positional — it's only settable as `--name=value`.

description.description: CLI Paths feature. Longer explanation shown in a command's `--help` output — `label` is usually too short for that. Not shown anywhere in the GUI form (label already covers that).

date_mode.description: date only. What the date picker popup asks for.

date_range.description: date only. Picks a start AND end value instead of one. The parameter itself ({{name}}) always carries the start; the end is injected as {{name.end}} (same convention as a collection-backed select's {{param.field}}).

date_format.description: date only. How the picked value is written into the command. "custom" uses date_format_custom instead of a fixed preset.

date_format_custom.description: date only, and only read when date_format is "custom". Qt date/time token template (yyyy, MM, dd, HH, mm, ss...).

group.description: Any type. Optional group name. Parameters sharing the exact same group are bundled into one collapsible section (collapsed by default) in the parameter-fill dialog, instead of appearing loose.

name.description: Required — a responder without one is discarded on import.

pattern.description: Regex matched against the output; capture groups available as \1, \2... in response.

hooks.description: Other commands to run before/after/on cleanup — referenced by NAME (not id), resolved against commands in the SAME package. A name that doesn't match any command is silently ignored (logged), never breaks the import.

name.description: Referenced by a parameter's "collection" key using this exact name.

folder.description: Target subfolder, same convention as a command's "folder".

schema.description: Columns. Omit to use the default [key, value] schema.

entries.description: Rows. SENSITIVE if the file is meant to be shared/committed — an entry can hold real data (tokens, credentials pasted in for testing), except for values under a field marked "secret" in the schema above, which Kai's own exporter always strips. Consider exporting the schema only (omit this key) for anything versioned, or marking the sensitive field(s) "secret".

name.description: Stable key, used in {{collection.<name>}} and in entries[].values.

secret.description: Masked as a password field in the UI. ALWAYS stripped from export, regardless of whether entries are otherwise included — the only way to take a secret value out of Kai is to copy it by hand.
